transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. I came in because I just keep getting these nagging thoughts that I forgot something important. It's usually about things like leaving my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or... or maybe not setting up my classroom materials safely for my students. And the thing is, even when I know I probably handled it fine, the doubt just keeps popping back into my head.
When those doubts come up, do you find yourself checking things over and over to feel sure?

Yeah, I do. Um, before I leave the house, or when I'm leaving my classroom at the end of the day, I’ll go back over the same things a few times. I check the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans... or sometimes I just silently replay what I did in my head. I basically just keep doing it until I feel calm enough to actually move on. It's frustrating because it definitely makes me run late sometimes, but I just need to feel sure before I can walk away.
Do these thoughts feel unwanted and intrusive, like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?

Yeah, they definitely do. Like I was saying earlier, I really don't want to be worrying about my aunt's medicine or my classroom setup, but the thoughts just force their way in. Even when I'm sitting there knowing I probably handled everything fine, that nagging doubt just pops right back into my head completely on its own. I can't really just turn it off.
Do you feel that the amount of checking you do is more than the situation really requires?

Yeah, I definitely do. Like I mentioned a minute ago, going back over the same things a few times—checking the pill organizer, the stove, or my lesson plans—I know it's excessive. Logically, checking once should be plenty. But I still end up replaying what I did in my head or physically checking again and again until I finally feel calm enough to move on. It's definitely more than the situation requires, especially since I know it ends up making me run late for no good reason.
About how much time do these checking and replaying behaviors take up in a typical day?

Um, I'm not exactly sure how much time it takes up, honestly. I haven't really timed it or anything. It's just... a few minutes here and there, I guess? Like, maybe ten or fifteen minutes before I leave the house, and then a little bit of time at the end of the school day. It's not taking up hours and hours, but it's enough to make me run late sometimes, like I said. So, yeah, I don't have an exact number for you.
When you have these thoughts and checking urges, do you feel they are unreasonable or excessive?

Yeah, I do. I mean, I think I just said this, but I know it's excessive. Logically, I know checking my aunt's pills once or locking the door once is enough. It's totally unreasonable to have to go back and check it three or four times, or to sit there replaying it in my head. I know it doesn't make sense, but I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it anyway.
Did these thoughts and checking behaviors start after a particular stressful event or change in your life?

Um, no, I don't think so. I can't really pinpoint one specific thing that happened. It wasn't like there was a huge stressful event or a big life change right before it all started. It just sort of... crept up on me gradually, I guess. I just started noticing that I was doing it more and more over time, rather than it starting all at once after something bad happened.
Outside of these checking-related thoughts, do you find yourself worrying a lot about many other parts of your life?

No, not really. I mean, I have normal worries, I guess. Like just regular stuff about my class or paying bills and things like that. But I don't feel like I worry excessively about everything else. It's really just... just those specific checking things that get stuck in my head. The rest of my life is pretty normal, stress-wise.
